questions.text: Who is the intended user of the Comprehension Checkpoint this spec describes?
options: The developer who just finished writing or reviewing a feature spec
End users of the software being specified
questions.expected_answer: The developer who just finished writing/reviewing a feature spec.md (whether they wrote it themselves or an AI drafted it from their description), per User Story 1.
questions.source_heading: User Story 1 - Take the comprehension checkpoint on a finished spec (Priority: P1)

questions.text: What must happen if spec.md doesn't have enough established content to truthfully support a question at some difficulty level?
questions.expected_answer: The system must propose a repair or clarification to spec.md and obtain the developer's explicit approval before applying it, rather than asking an untruthful question or editing spec.md silently.
questions.source_heading: User Story 3 - The checkpoint never tests information the spec doesn't establish (Priority: P2); FR-003

questions.text: Suppose a developer answers a checkpoint question by describing how they'd implement it (e.g. naming a specific database table) instead of addressing the spec-level question. How should the system respond?
questions.expected_answer: Treat it as out of scope for the checkpoint (that belongs to planning, not this check), coach the developer back toward spec-level content, and re-ask rather than grading the implementation-detail answer as correct or incorrect.

questions.text: Trace what happens across a checkpoint session if a developer answers the same question incorrectly many times in a row, right up until they explicitly ask to skip it. What gets recorded, and does the session end?
questions.expected_answer: Coaching and retrying continues indefinitely at that difficulty level with no attempt cap and no automatic reveal. The developer can explicitly skip/reveal that one question, which is recorded as skipped rather than passed, and the session continues to the next level rather than ending.

questions.text: Two of this spec's guarantees are: (a) a developer only advances past a level after a judged-correct answer or an explicit skip, and (b) nothing about a session is ever written to the repository. Is there tension between these when a developer declines a proposed spec.md repair, and how does the spec resolve it?
questions.expected_answer: No lasting tension: an approved repair is a deliberate edit to spec.md's own content, distinct from session bookkeeping, so it doesn't conflict with guarantee (b). If a repair is declined, the checkpoint substitutes different already-established content for that level, or states plainly that none exists — it never persists a failed/partial result and never asks an untruthful question, so both guarantees hold simultaneously.
